hourly.summary: Manchester United fans are in full-blown crisis mode after a 2-0 loss to Chelsea extended their winless run to nine games. The forum is united in despair over a perceived endless cycle of managerial changes yielding the same underperforming players — Martinez, Maguire, Dalot, Bruno, Cunha — who face zero accountability while the hierarchy (Carrick, Wilcox, Berrada) dithers. Comparisons to Ferguson's early struggles only deepen the gloom: "there are no Fergies left" and the club appears trapped in a "relentless, unending rotation" of failure, with supporters demanding a total Arsenal-style clearout rather than another reheated rebuild.

daily.summary: Sentiment plummeted from pre-match apprehension (4/10) to full-blown catastrophe (2/10) across the day as a 2-0 loss to Chelsea — sparked by Lisandro Martinez's 83-second double-yellow — extended United's winless run to nine games, their worst start since 1988, and dropped the club into the relegation zone. Post-match summaries converge on total systemic collapse: Carrick's authority evaporated, INEOS and the Glazers face unified fury, the squad is labelled 'rotting', and relegation is openly discussed as a desirable path to ownership change.

weekly.summary: Manchester United fan sentiment remained locked in a sustained, week-long catastrophe with scores barely moving from 2/10 across all seven days. The 4-1 Champions League thrashing by Como and a 3-0 home humiliation to Bournemouth bookended a period defined by total loss of faith in Carrick, the Glazers, and INEOS, with the mood hardening from grim resignation into open revolt — anti-ownership chants, serious relegation talk, and gallows humour as the only coping mechanism. No meaningful improvement occurred; the week ended in full-blown freefall.
